data_description.important_note: This dataset from MODIS Terra and Aqua satellites (MCD19A2) provides daily aerosol optical depth measurements crucial for detecting and tracking dust storm events. Dust storms are characterized by elevated AOD values (typically >0.5) over arid and semi-arid regions. The Multi-Angle Implementation of Atmospheric Correction (MAIAC) algorithm provides improved spatial resolution and accuracy over bright desert surfaces where dust originates.
analytical_capabilities: Dust storm outbreak detection and tracking
Dust source region identification and characterization
Dust storm frequency and intensity climatology
Dust emission and atmospheric loading quantification
Air quality and visibility impact assessment during dust events

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) dimensionless at 550nm wavelength; values >0.5 typically indicate moderate to heavy aerosol loading; dust storms often produce AOD >1.0 to >3.0.
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Combine high AOD values with low Ångström exponent (<0.6) to distinguish coarse-mode dust aerosols from fine-mode pollution or smoke; use temporal change detection to identify dust outbreak events.

data_description.data_source: NASA MODIS MAIAC Aerosol Product (MCD19A2) via Google Earth Engine
